preamble: A labialized or rounded-vowel-adjacent [x] can become the labiodental [f], with the lip rounding taking over as the place of articulation. In late Middle English, word-final [x] after back rounded vowels became /f/ in a set of words such as tough, enough and laugh; other words with the same ending lost the [x] instead. Traditional Scots and northern English dialects keep [x] in this position.

examples.from: Middle English tough, toȝ [x] (Old English tōh)
Middle English laughen, laghen [x] (Old English hliehhan)
